verdicts.note: (not flagged verify) IMSLP 'Cherry Blossom': violin & piano, F major, work title 'Kirschblute' with alternative title 'Fleur de Cerisier'. Published under Schütt's pseudonym H. (Henri) Marling: Monte-Carlo: Cincaf-Music Co., 1923, plate C.M.C. 5 (same plate as N2, so probably one print). Pseudonym 'Henri Marling' is confirmed by de.wikipedia and the Oesterreichisches Musiklexikon; the only edition found is this late print, so the evidence is thin but real. Which language the score's own title uses is not stated.

(not flagged verify) IMSLP 'Midinette': violin & piano, published under the pseudonym H. Marling: Monte-Carlo: Cincaf-Music Co., 1923, plate C.M.C. 5 (same plate as N1). Key not stated. Thin evidence (single late edition), see N1.

(not flagged verify) 4 Morceaux, Op. 52, violin & piano, Berlin: N. Simrock, 1897, plate 10856, dedicated to Bernhard Dessau. IMSLP lists the four pieces in this order: 1 Ariette, 2 Serenata, 3 Mélodie-Berceuse, 4 Mazurka; queued titles N3-N6 match.
(not flagged verify) Piece 2 of 4 Morceaux, Op. 52 (Simrock 1897); title matches IMSLP.
(not flagged verify) Piece 3 of 4 Morceaux, Op. 52 (Simrock 1897); title matches IMSLP.
(not flagged verify) Piece 4 of 4 Morceaux, Op. 52 (Simrock 1897); title matches IMSLP.

(not flagged verify) 2 Morceaux, Op. 53, violin & piano, Berlin: N. Simrock, 1897 (plates 10878 and 10879). IMSLP piece order: 1 Elégie slave, 2 Valse-Bluette. Elégie slave was also issued by Carl Fischer, New York, 1917 (plate 20625, ed. Carl Friedberg).

(not flagged verify) Piece 2 of 2 Morceaux, Op. 53 (Simrock 1897, plate 10879). Not to be confused with the piano solo 'Valse-bluette' (Leipzig: Bosworth, 1905, no opus number), which is a different piece.

(not flagged verify) Suite No. 1 in D minor, Op. 44, violin & piano, Berlin: N. Simrock, 1894, plate 10232; dedicated to Arnold Rosé. Four movements: Allegro risoluto; Scherzo (Vivace); Canzonetta con variazioni; Rondo à la russe. Also listed in Wikipedia's selected works.

(not flagged verify) Suite No. 2 in E major, Op. 61, violin & piano, Berlin: N. Simrock, 1901, plate 11553; dedicated to Émile Sauret. Four movements: Allegro moderato; Scherzo; Moto amoroso; Finale. de.wikipedia also lists a 'Suite No. 3 for piano and violin, Op. 86', but IMSLP has no such page and I found no edition, so it is not proposed as a gap.

(not flagged verify) Violin Sonata in G major, Op. 26, violin & piano, Hamburg/Leipzig: D. Rahter, 1888, plate 2803; dedicated to Julius Winkler. Three movements: Allegro risoluto; Intermezzo (Poco andante - Quasi allegro - Tempo I); Poco allegro moderato. Appears only on IMSLP, not in the Wikipedia work lists.

gap_check_note: No confirmed gaps. Sources: IMSLP composer category (87 works; I opened the violin-tagged pages plus Elegie, Arioso Op. 33, Romance appassionato Op. 91, 2 Canzones Op. 96, Andante cantabile and Scherzino Op. 79, 2 Airs Op. 39, none of which is a violin work), en/de Wikipedia work lists and the Oesterreichisches Musiklexikon. Unconfirmed: de.wikipedia lists a 'Suite No. 3 for piano and violin, Op. 86' (no IMSLP page, no edition found), and the Musiklexikon mentions unspecified 'Violinstücke'; neither was added. No violin concerto or arrangements by notable violinists found. WebSearch was unavailable (session budget used up), so only direct page fetches were used.

existing_issues.issue: 'À la bien-aimée' is originally a solo-piano piece (No. 2 of Papillons d'amour, Op. 59, Berlin: Simrock, 1900: 1 À mignonne, 2 À la bien-aimée, 3 À ma chérie, 4 À mon amie, 5 À la capricieuse). The violin & piano version on IMSLP is an arrangement by an unnamed arranger (New York: Appleton, ca. 1919, ed. Albert Ernest Wier), so house style would mark it as an arrangement rather than 'from Papillons d'amour'.
existing_issues.suggested_title: À la bien-aimée, Op. 59 No. 2 (orig. piano)
